title: Weekly MLS Winners and Losers: Matt Turner Makes Strong USMNT Case
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach Lowy12:15 PM EDTMatt Turner continued his stellar performance between the posts. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesWelcome to a new feature from Sports Illustrated that analyzes the biggest winners and losers from the week’s Major League Soccer action as the 2026 playoffs grow increasingly close.
With the league’s Nov. 7th Decision Day looming, the weekend’s play was bound to feature plenty of tight finishes and upset wins. It did not disappoint.

The Colorado Rapids narrowly clung above the playoff line with a win against Western Conference leaders Vancouver Whitecaps. Meanwhile, Austin FC stormed to a late comeback win at Sporting Kansas City, and San Diego FC and New York City FC equalized in the dying seconds against the Seattle Sounders and Orlando City, respectively.

Nashville SC secured their maiden Supporters’ Shield with a comprehensive 2–0 win against CF Montréal. The youthful New York Red Bulls put an end to Inter Miami's three-game winning streak, halting Lionel Messi and Co. in their tracks. And as usual, El Tráfico lived up to the billing with a pulsating 2–2 draw.

Across North America, there were several players who came up clutch for their teams, delivering vital goals, incisive passes, game-saving tackles and world-class saves. There were also quite a few who failed to get the job done, leaving fans wanting more out of their underwhelming individual displays.
Here are the week’s biggest winners and losers.

After suffering a heartbreaking penalty shootout defeat to St. Louis CITY in the U.S. Open Cup final last week, Columbus Crew needed to bounce back. They did just that, prevailing 4–2 against Toronto FC in a pivotal match between two teams on the fringes of the playoff positions.

Columbus raced to an early start with goals from Gonzalo Tapia and Malte Amundsen, the latter heading home Dylan Chambost’s corner kick. It was more of the same after the restart, with Chambost playing a corner short before whipping in a delightful delivery for Amundsen to tap in.

The French midfielder put the game to bed after unselfishly teeing up substitute Brooks Lennon's goal, matching his assist tally for the season in just 90 minutes. Chambost became just the sixth player in club history to deliver three assists in a single match. While Toronto attempted a late comeback after the expulsion of Sekou Bangoura, it was too little, too late as Columbus made it six wins from eight.

With two goals in tonight’s victory, @FCDallas' Petar Musa reached 56 goals across his first three @MLS seasons, tying Raúl Díaz Arce (1996-98) for the third-most goals by a player in his first three seasons in league history. pic.twitter.com/clWHsMkJLj

Lionel Messi has won nine Golden Boots across his time in La Liga and MLS, second only to Josef Bican in soccer history; however, if he is to claim the coveted No. 10 this year, he will have to overcome some serious competition from FC Dallas’ Petar Musa, whose career-best 22 goals this season are inching close to Messi’s 25.

After bagging a last-second equalizer at rivals Houston Dynamo last week, Musa continued his goal-scoring heroics. Musa broke the deadlock in the 82nd minute against the San Jose Earthquakes, patiently waiting at the edge of the box for a cutback before deftly firing into the right corner. He then doubled the game’s scoring from the penalty spot five minutes later, before teammate Santiago Moreno added a third unanswered.

Six years after becoming the Czech First League’s youngest-ever top scorer, Musa finds himself in another heated Golden Boot race. The Croatian striker has already obliterated Dallas’ single-season record for goals, but now, can he pip Messi to the Golden Boot?
Until the final whistle. 😤Matt Turner's massive save in the 16th minute of stoppage time is your @MichelobULTRA Superior Moment of the Match. pic.twitter.com/BpaoZFr1Wz

He may have lost his starting spot to Matt Freese and is now facing competition from young guns like Diego Kochen, Chris Brady, and Brian Schwake. But even at 32 years old, Matt Turner is showing that he’s still got plenty of fuel left in the tank and is capable of reclaiming his position as the U.S. men’s national team’s top shot-stopper.

Not called up to USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino's roster last month, Turner suffered a second-straight 3–0 defeat with the New England Revolution immediately after the international break. However, he has since responded in style with heroic displays against FC Cincinnati, Chicago Fire and Philadelphia Union, making 13 saves during that run.

For the third straight match, New England Revolution secured victory despite conceding more expected goals. He was at his brilliant best in the City of Brotherly Love, tipping over a ferocious shot from Agustin Anello and ensuring that Philadelphia’s unbeaten streak was snapped after 15 matches.
